head: working-tree
subject: gRPC owned unary response message
change: UnaryResponseOptions gains owned_message backed by grpc.OwnedResponseMessage, prefix-reserved storage that a handler serializes into directly. An identity unary response hands that exact allocation to the HTTP/2 writer, removing the framed staging copy of the whole response; compressed responses still allocate a separate framed buffer, and the borrowed message field keeps the existing staging path. The buffer is borrowed for the synchronous write and remains caller-owned, so a persistent server reuses one allocation across responses.

tests.unit: src/grpc/runtime_tests.zig runs a real h2c server that fills one OwnedResponseMessage payload and answers two consecutive unary calls from the same buffer, verifying both client responses while the caller retains storage.

focused_gate.command: zig build test-lib -Dtest-filter='owned unary response' --summary all

benchmark.workload: 256 KiB full-byte-validated unary round trips, 20 warmups, 200 measured calls

notes: The benchmark is an internal API-shape comparison with the same binary: only the server response ownership changes. The borrowed path stages prefix plus payload and allocates a framed buffer per response; the owned path reuses one prefix-reserved buffer and performs no per-response copy or allocation. A response with both message and owned_message is rejected as InvalidMessageCount, and compressed responses still take the framed fallback.
